(1) IHF and supercoiling both activate the ilvPG operon promoter, but by distinct mechanisms, and that (2) IHF binds equally well to relaxed or supercoiled DNA.

IHF and increased supercoiling both activate transcription from the ilvgP promoter, but IHF and supercoiling do not act by the same mechanism and IHF binds with equivalent affinity to its target sites on both relaxed and supercooled DNAs.
IHF activates transcription from the promoter by altering the structure of the supercoiled DNA helix in its binding site, which facilitates open complex formation at the downstream promoter region.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the mechanism by which IHF and DNA supercoiling influence the transcription of the ilvPG operon in Escherichia Coli.
the effects of IHF binding on transcription and how DNA supercoiling influences these effects.
how the structure of DNA influences gene expression.

the activation of transcription from the ilvgp promoter by IHF is a direct consequence of the distortion of the DNA helical structure in the region upstream of the IHF binding site.

IHF activates transcription by distorting the DNA structure in the upstream region of a negatively supercoiled DNA helix in a way that increases the probability of open complex formation in the downstream promoter.
